quizName: DMV Practice Test #10 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Riding directly alongside another vehicle:

options.text: Can place you in the driver's blind spot.
Is better than riding behind the other vehicle.
Is safe because it limits your escape routes.
Should only be done during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can place you in the driver's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Do not ride directly alongside another vehicle. The driver may not see you in their blind spot. They could move into your lane without warning. Riding alongside also blocks your escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: When making a turn:

options.text: There is less traction available for stopping.
There is more traction available for stopping.
Stopping is no different than making a stop on a straightaway.
Stopping should never be attempted.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is less traction available for stopping.
questions.explanation: You can brake while turning, but be very careful. When a motorcycle leans to turn, some traction is used for turning. This means less traction is available for braking.

questions.question: Why should you use both the front and rear brakes every time you slow or stop?

options.text: Using only one brake will cause the brakes to wear unevenly.
It develops good braking habits for emergency situations.
Using both brakes is the only way to slow down a motorcycle.
The brakes only work when both are applied.

questions.correctAnswerText: It develops good braking habits for emergency situations.
questions.explanation: Using both brakes during normal stops builds a habit. This habit will help you in emergencies when using both brakes may be critical.

questions.question: Goggles can:

options.text: Protect your eyes and your face.
Protect your face but not your eyes.
Protect your eyes, but not your face.
Not protect your face or eyes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect your eyes, but not your face.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes. Only a face shield can protect your entire face during a crash.

questions.question: Most crashes happen:

options.text: Far from home.
On short trips.
On long rides.
Several hours into the ride.

questions.correctAnswerText: On short trips.
questions.explanation: Most crashes happen on trips shorter than five miles. They occur just a few minutes after the rider starts out.

questions.question: When approaching railroad tracks that cross your lane at an angle, it is usually:

options.text: Safest to ride straight within your lane to cross the tracks.
Dangerous to ride straight within your lane to cross the tracks.
Not safe to cross tracks on a motorcycle.
Safest to cross the tracks by riding on the shoulder of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Safest to ride straight within your lane to cross the tracks.
questions.explanation: When railroad tracks cross your lane at an angle, ride straight across them while staying in your lane. Turning to cross at a 90-degree angle is dangerous because you could move into another lane of traffic.

questions.question: When you are being passed, you should:

options.text: Ride in the center portion of the lane.
Ride in the left portion of the lane.
Ride in the right portion of the lane.
Weave among the three portions of the lane as the vehicle passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, ride in the center of your lane. Riding on the side nearest the passing vehicle increases collision risk. Riding on the far side may make the other driver merge back into your lane too early.

questions.question: A helmet will not provide the best possible protection:

options.text: If it is certified by the DOT.
If it fits snugly.
If it is free of defects.
If it has cracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: If it has cracks.
questions.explanation: A helmet must meet U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards and fit snugly to provide maximum protection. It should have no defects like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: When passing a row of parked cars to your right when there is no oncoming traffic to your left, you should:

options.text: Stay toward the right side of your lane.
Stay toward the left side of your lane.
Look to your left frequently.
Use your rearview mirrors more frequently than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay toward the left side of your lane.
questions.explanation: When passing parked cars, stay on the side of your lane away from the cars. This protects you from car doors opening or people stepping out between cars. Stay in the center if oncoming traffic is present.

questions.question: Which option gives a rider the best protection?

options.text: Goggles
A face shield
A windshield
Eyeglasses

questions.correctAnswerText: A face shield
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face if you crash. Goggles only protect your eyes, not your whole face. A windshield or eyeglasses do not replace goggles or a face shield.

questions.question: Where should you place a load on your motorcycle?

options.text: As low as possible
As high as possible
Behind the rear axle
On one side of the motorcycle

questions.correctAnswerText: As low as possible
questions.explanation: Keep loads low and secure them with saddlebags. Placing loads high on the back of the seat raises the center of gravity and throws off the motorcycle's balance. Always spread loads equally on both sides of the motorcycle.

questions.question: If your motorcycle's chain or belt breaks, what happens?

options.text: The rear wheel suddenly gets more power.
The rear wheel suddenly loses power.
The front wheel suddenly loses power.
The front wheel suddenly gets more power.

questions.correctAnswerText: The rear wheel suddenly loses power.
questions.explanation: If the chain or belt breaks, the rear wheel will immediately stop receiving power.

questions.question: If a small animal enters your lane in traffic, what should you do?

options.text: Swerve into other lanes if needed to avoid the animal.
Switch lanes as quickly as possible.
Stay in your lane.
Flash your lights to scare the animal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your lane.
questions.explanation: Avoid hitting an animal safely. In traffic, stay in your lane. Swerving into another lane can cause you to hit another vehicle. Hitting a small animal is safer than crashing with another car.

questions.question: What is engine braking?

options.text: It is illegal.
It is slowing down by turning the engine off.
It is slowing down by downshifting.
It damages the engine and is not encouraged.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is slowing down by downshifting.
questions.explanation: When you shift to a lower gear, it works like applying the brakes. This is called engine braking.

questions.question: When making a normal stop, what should you do?

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.
Use only the rear brake to save the front brake.
Use only the front brake to save the rear brake.
Squeeze the front brake sharply.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when slowing or stopping. Practicing this habit makes it easier to brake quickly in an emergency.

questions.question: How often should you use both brakes when slowing or stopping?

options.text: Only if the pavement is wet.
Infrequently.
Only when riding in the city.
Every time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every time.
questions.explanation: Using both brakes gives you the most stopping power. Use both brakes every time you slow or stop.

questions.question: What lane position should you choose?

options.text: One that minimizes your space cushion and makes you visible.
One that maximizes your space cushion and makes you visible.
One that increases road hazards and lets others pass you.
One that decreases road hazards and lets you follow closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: One that maximizes your space cushion and makes you visible.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and be seen. It helps you avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. Your lane position should keep other riders from sharing your lane and give you an escape route. Choose a position that maximizes your space cushion.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, what should you do?

options.text: Turn both your head and shoulders.
Turn just your head, not your shoulders.
Use only your mirrors.
Move only your eyes, not your head.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head, not your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Look ahead to where you want to go through the turn. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: What is Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) designed to do?

options.text: Prevent skidding and wheel lock-up.
Prevent brakes from working on dry roads.
Apply brakes automatically.
Warn you when brake pads need replacing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent skidding and wheel lock-up.
questions.explanation: ABS is designed to stop your wheels from skidding and locking up during hard braking. When you apply maximum pressure to both brake controls, electronic sensors detect if a wheel will lock. The system then releases and re-applies brake pressure to keep maximum braking power.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's stopping power comes from the front brake?

options.text: About one-quarter
About one-half
About three-quarters
All of it

questions.correctAnswerText: About three-quarters
questions.explanation: The front brake is stronger than the rear brake. It provides about three-quarters of a motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: What do studies show about motorcycles with headlights on during the day?

options.text: They are harder to see than other vehicles.
They are more visible to other drivers than with headlights off.
They confuse other drivers.
They are less safe than with headlights off.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are more visible to other drivers than with headlights off.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on whenever you ride. A motorcycle with its headlight on is twice as likely to be noticed by other drivers during the day.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, how should you adjust for the extra weight?

options.text: Ride slower than usual.
Stay closer to the car in front of you.
Ride faster than usual.
Brake a little later than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride slower than usual.
questions.explanation: Extra weight makes your motorcycle need more time to speed up, slow down, and turn. Reduce your speed, start slowing earlier than normal, and increase your following distance.

questions.question: What does eye contact with another driver mean?

options.text: The driver has seen you.
It does not guarantee the driver will yield to you.
The driver will always yield to you.
It may anger the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not guarantee the driver will yield to you.
questions.explanation: Do not rely on eye contact. Drivers often look directly at motorcyclists but still fail to see them.

questions.question: What usually causes a motorcycle to move into another lane while turning?

options.text: Taking the turn too fast.
Lanes that are too narrow.
Poor steering skills.
Lanes that are too wide.

questions.correctAnswerText: Taking the turn too fast.
questions.explanation: Going too fast into a curve or turn may cause you to cross into another lane or leave the road.
